This Insight feature explores the 'living apart together' (LAT) phenomenon, where long-term partners maintain separate residences to preserve personal routines and independence, often finding it strengthens their bond.

The Bright Side:
It validates diverse relationship structures, reducing the stigma for those who find traditional cohabitation stifling or incompatible with their personal needs.

By prioritizing individual autonomy, these couples reduce domestic friction. This transparency about personal needs fosters a more stable, voluntary connection rather than one built on forced compromise.
